questions.q: What four layers does Singh say hide the root of a problem?
a: A pretext, an excuse, a self-told lie and past trauma
Fear, anger, denial and regret
Blame, shame, guilt and avoidance
Doubt, delay, distraction and pride
questions.why: Lesson one describes peeling back the story you tell others, the excuse you tell yourself, a convincing lie and old trauma.

questions.q: What does Singh say about people who try to bring you down?
a: Their criticism usually reflects their own issues
They are usually right and worth listening to
They should be argued with until they stop
They deserve a public response every time
questions.why: The summary advises shaking such people off because what they say is mostly a reflection of themselves.

questions.q: What is the first step toward achieving a dream, according to Singh?
a: Picture the outcome in complete detail
Find a mentor who has done it before
Save enough money to quit your job
Tell everyone about your plan
questions.why: Lesson two says to imagine the desired life down to the last detail, perhaps with a vision board or daily visualization.

questions.q: How does Singh suggest fighting procrastination?
a: Set deadlines for yourself and stick to them
Wait until you feel truly motivated
Work on several tasks at once
Reward yourself before starting
questions.why: Lesson three says self-imposed deadlines keep you on track and turn stress into something useful.

questions.q: What kind of circle does Singh say you should build around yourself?
a: Positive people who lift you up and keep you focused
Powerful people who can open doors for you
Honest critics who point out your flaws
Independent people who need nothing from you
questions.why: Lesson three recommends a constructive circle that shares your excitement and helps you stay on track.
